name: David Lett
summary: Moved to Oregon in 1965 after studying viticulture at UC Davis and planted the Willamette Valley's first Pinot noir. Founder of The Eyrie Vineyards and the first to grow Pinot gris in Oregon.

sources.title: David Lett, founder of Oregon Pinot Noir, dies (Decanter)

name: Diana Lett
summary: Co-founded The Eyrie Vineyards with her husband David Lett; together they produced the first Pinot noir in the Willamette Valley.

name: Jason Lett
summary: Son of David and Diana Lett. Took over as winemaker and vineyard manager at The Eyrie Vineyards in 2005 and is now its president.

name: Earl Jones
summary: Co-founder with Hilda Jones of Abacela in the Umpqua Valley, where they planted Oregon's first Tempranillo in 1995. He co-petitioned for the Southern Oregon AVA and served on the Oregon Wine Board from 2003 to 2009.

sources.title: Past Oregon Wine Board Directors (Oregon Wine Board)

name: Hilda Jones
summary: Co-founder and co-owner of Abacela with Earl Jones; the two received the Oregon wine industry's Lifetime Achievement Award in 2015. She served on the Oregon Wine Board from 2016 to 2021.

sources.title: Past Oregon Wine Board Directors (Oregon Wine Board)

name: Gregory V. Jones
summary: Research climatologist specializing in the climatology of viticulture and son of Abacela founder Earl Jones. He co-petitioned for the Southern Oregon AVA, held posts at Southern Oregon University and Linfield, and became Abacela's CEO in 2021.

name: Ed King Jr.
summary: Founded King Estate in 1991 with his son Ed King III, after a career that began in aircraft electronics design.

sources.title: Ed King III, Co-CEO & Co-Founder (King Estate)

name: Ed King III
summary: Co-founder and co-CEO of King Estate, which he started with his father Ed King Jr. in 1991.

sources.title: Ed King III, Co-CEO & Co-Founder (King Estate)

name: Frank Wisnovsky
summary: Bought 76 acres in the Applegate Valley in 1971 and planted grapes the following year, re-establishing the Valley View name that Peter Britt had used in the nineteenth century.

name: Dick Troon
summary: Planted some of Southern Oregon's first post-Prohibition wine grapes in the Applegate Valley in 1972 and gave his name to Troon Vineyard.

sources.title: Oral history interview with Dick Troon (Oregon Historical Society)

name: Scott Henry
summary: Oregon State-trained aerospace engineer who planted a vineyard at Umpqua in 1972 and opened Henry Estate Winery in 1978. In 1982 he devised the split-canopy Scott Henry Trellis System, now used worldwide.

sources.title: Oregon winemaker Scott Henry dies at age 86 (Capital Press)
Henry Estate Winery patriarch dies at age 86 (The News-Review)
Henry Estate Winery Collection (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Philippe Girardet
summary: Swiss-raised founder, with his wife Bonnie, of Girardet Vineyards and Winery at Tenmile in the Umpqua Valley. He introduced Baco noir to the valley in 1971 and bottled Oregon's first 100% Baco noir in 1990.

sources.title: Philippe Girardet, Founder of Girardet Vineyards and Winery, Passes Away at 96 (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Christophe Baron
summary: Winegrower from a Champagne family who bought stony ground at Milton-Freewater in 1996, named the venture Cayuse and planted Cailloux Vineyard in 1997.

name: Stephen Cary
summary: Longtime winemaker at Yamhill Valley Vineyards and one of the originators of the Steamboat Pinot Noir Conference. He also proposed the 1985 Oregon-Burgundy Challenge tasting in New York.

sources.title: In Memoriam: Stephen Cary (Oregon Wine Press)
Steamboat Conference History, by Stephen J. Cary (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Barney Watson
summary: Instructor and Enology Extension Specialist at Oregon State University for 28 years, who worked on bringing grape clones into the Oregon wine industry.

sources.title: Barney Watson interview (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Robert Drouhin
summary: Head of the Burgundy house Maison Joseph Drouhin who first visited Oregon in 1961. In 1987 he bought land in the Dundee Hills and established Domaine Drouhin Oregon.

sources.title: Profiles in Pinot Noir: Domaine Drouhin (Wine Spectator)

name: Véronique Drouhin-Boss
summary: Daughter of Robert Drouhin, trained in enology at the University of Dijon. She interned with three Oregon wine families in 1986 and has been winemaker at Domaine Drouhin Oregon since its first vintage in 1988.

sources.title: The French woman of Oregon, Véronique Drouhin-Boss (BKWine Magazine)
Profiles in Pinot Noir: Domaine Drouhin (Wine Spectator)

name: Ken Wright
summary: Winemaker who moved from California to Oregon and founded Panther Creek Cellars in 1986, then Ken Wright Cellars in Carlton in 1994. He was also the first winemaker at Domaine Serene and petitioned to shorten the Yamhill-Carlton AVA name.

sources.title: Ken Wright lecture announcement (Linfield University news)
Ken Wright Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Michael G. Etzel
summary: Founder and longtime manager of Beaux Frères on Ribbon Ridge, which he started on a former pig farm with backing from his brother-in-law, the wine critic Robert Parker. He worked harvests at Ponzi Vineyards while establishing the vineyard.

sources.title: The Birth and Building of Beaux Frères (Wine Spectator)

name: Robert M. Parker Jr.
summary: Maryland-based wine critic who founded The Wine Advocate in 1978. In the late 1980s he invested in the Oregon vineyard that became Beaux Frères with his brother-in-law Michael Etzel, and promised never to review its wines.

name: Dick Shea
summary: Former Wall Street trader who planted Shea Vineyard near Carlton in 1989 with two East Coast partners, later buying them out. He sells most of the fruit to other wineries and also runs his own label, Shea Wine Cellars, with his wife Deirdre.

sources.title: Shea Vineyard and Shea Wine Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Ted Casteel
summary: Co-founder and longtime vineyard manager of Bethel Heights Vineyard, and twin brother of Terry Casteel. He co-founded the LIVE sustainable-viticulture certification program and co-petitioned for the Eola-Amity Hills AVA.

name: Terry Casteel
summary: Co-founder of Bethel Heights Vineyard and twin brother of Ted Casteel. He took over the winemaking in 1984 and later handed it to his son Ben.

name: Paul Gerrie
summary: Pittsburgh engineer who founded Cristom Vineyards with his wife Eileen in 1992 after attending the International Pinot Noir Celebration in 1991. He retired in 2012 and passed ownership to his children.

name: Steve Doerner
summary: UC Davis biochemistry graduate who spent 14 years at Calera Wine Company in California before Paul Gerrie hired him as Cristom Vineyards' winemaker in 1992. He later became a partner in the winery.

name: Rollin Soles
summary: Texas-born winemaker with a master's in enology from UC Davis who co-founded Argyle Winery with Brian Croser in 1987 and was its winemaker until 2013. He and his wife Corby Stonebraker-Soles own ROCO Winery.

sources.title: Rollin Soles Relinquishes Winemaker Title at Argyle (Wine Spectator)

name: Brian Croser
summary: Australian winemaker and founder of Petaluma in South Australia. He co-founded Argyle Winery in Dundee with Rollin Soles, who had worked with him at Petaluma.

sources.title: Rollin Soles Relinquishes Winemaker Title at Argyle (Wine Spectator)

name: Harry Peterson-Nedry
summary: Planted Ridgecrest Vineyards in 1980, the first vineyard in what became the Ribbon Ridge AVA, and founded Chehalem winery in 1990. He was a cited author of the Ribbon Ridge AVA petition.

sources.title: Bill Stoller, Oregon Vintner and Philanthropist, Dies at Age 74 (Wine Spectator)

name: Jim Bernau
summary: Founder of Willamette Valley Vineyards, where he began planting Pinot noir in the Salem Hills in 1983. As a young lobbyist he represented the Oregon Winegrowers in passing the 1981 legislation that created the Oregon Wine Advisory Board.

sources.title: The Jim Bernau story (Oregon State University College of Business)

name: Lynn Penner-Ash
summary: UC Davis graduate who worked at Stag's Leap Wine Cellars, Domaine Chandon and Chateau St. Jean before joining Rex Hill in 1988, where she became president. She started Penner-Ash Wine Cellars with her husband Ron in 1998.

sources.title: Penner-Ash Wine Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Larry Stone
summary: Master Sommelier who managed Evening Land Vineyards until January 2012, then bought the Janzen farm beside Seven Springs Vineyard and founded Lingua Franca. He sold Lingua Franca to Constellation Brands in 2022.

sources.title: Larry Stone Returns to Oregon with New Vineyard and Winery (Wine Spectator)
Exclusive: Constellation Buys Oregon's Lingua Franca (Wine Spectator)

name: Dominique Lafon
summary: Burgundy vigneron who consulted for Evening Land Vineyards in Oregon and later worked with Larry Stone as consultant at Lingua Franca.

sources.title: Larry Stone Returns to Oregon with New Vineyard and Winery (Wine Spectator)

name: Josh Bergström
summary: General manager, winemaker and vineyard manager of Bergström Wines, which he started with his parents in 1999 after completing a postgraduate program in viticulture and enology in Burgundy.

name: Ken Evenstad
summary: Minnesota pharmaceutical executive who founded Domaine Serene in the Dundee Hills with his wife Grace. The couple bought Château de la Crée in Burgundy in 2015.

sources.title: Ken Evenstad, Co-Founder of Oregon's Domaine Serene Winery, Dies at 77 (Wine Spectator)

name: Grace Evenstad
summary: Co-founder and owner of Domaine Serene, which she established in the Dundee Hills with her husband Ken Evenstad in 1989.

sources.title: Ken Evenstad, Co-Founder of Oregon's Domaine Serene Winery, Dies at 77 (Wine Spectator)

name: Tony Rynders
summary: Winemaker who arrived in Oregon in 1994 as an assistant winemaker at Argyle, took over winemaking at Domaine Serene in 1998 and led it for about a decade. Bacchus Capital hired him to make the Panther Creek wines in 2013.

sources.title: Ken Wright and Panther Creek Cellars (Great Northwest Wine)
Panther Creek Cellars (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Bill Stoller
summary: Businessman who invested in Ridgecrest Vineyards in 1988 and was co-owner of Chehalem by 1993, becoming its sole owner in 2018. He also founded Stoller Family Estate on his family's former turkey farm in the Dundee Hills.

sources.title: Bill Stoller, Oregon Vintner and Philanthropist, Dies at Age 74 (Wine Spectator)

name: Ben Casteel
summary: Son of Terry Casteel and Marilyn Webb. He worked a harvest in Burgundy and spent five years at Rex Hill before succeeding his father as winemaker at Bethel Heights Vineyard.

name: Pat Dudley
summary: Co-founder and president of Bethel Heights Vineyard and wife of Ted Casteel. She co-founded Oregon Pinot Camp and is a former executive director of the International Pinot Noir Celebration.

name: Tom Gerrie
summary: Son of Cristom founders Paul and Eileen Gerrie. He joined the winery after graduating in 2007 and became its majority owner in 2012.

name: Nate Klostermann
summary: Rollin Soles' assistant at Argyle Winery for seven years before succeeding him as winemaker on 1 March 2013.

sources.title: Rollin Soles Relinquishes Winemaker Title at Argyle (Wine Spectator)

name: Mark Tarlov
summary: Former attorney and film producer who founded Evening Land Vineyards in 2005 and leased Seven Springs Vineyard in 2007. He left the company in January 2012.

sources.title: Evening Land Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)
Larry Stone Returns to Oregon with New Vineyard and Winery (Wine Spectator)

name: Richard Sommer
summary: Attended UC Davis and founded HillCrest Vineyard near Roseburg in 1961, where he planted Oregon's first Pinot noir. Sold the winery in 2003.

name: Charles Coury
summary: UC Davis graduate who arrived in northern Oregon in 1965 and planted Pinot noir and Alsatian varieties at Charles Coury Vineyards near Forest Grove, which he ran until 1978.

sources.title: Vineyards Established 1965-1971 (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Dick Erath
summary: California-born engineer who took classes at UC Davis in 1967, moved to the Willamette Valley in 1968 and planted his first vines near Newberg in 1969. Founded Erath Winery, which he sold to Ste. Michelle Wine Estates in 2006.

sources.title: Dick Erath, Willamette Valley pioneer, passes away at 87 (Northwest Wine Report)
Erath Winery Collection: historical note (Linfield / Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Cal Knudsen
summary: Lawyer and timber executive who bought a former walnut orchard in the Dundee Hills in 1971 and planted Knudsen Vineyards. Partner in Knudsen Erath Winery and later chairman of Argyle Winery from 1990 to 2007.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Pioneer Cal Knudsen Dies (Wine Spectator)
Dick Erath, Willamette Valley pioneer, passes away at 87 (Northwest Wine Report)

name: Dick Ponzi
summary: Engineer who founded Ponzi Vineyards with his wife Nancy in 1970 and was its winemaker until 1993. Founding member and first president of the Oregon Winegrowers Association and a co-founder of BridgePort Brewing.

name: Nancy Ponzi
summary: Co-founded Ponzi Vineyards with her husband Dick in 1970. Co-founded the International Pinot Noir Celebration in 1987 and Oregon Pinot Camp in 2000, and founded the vineyard-worker health program ¡Salud! in 1991.

name: Luisa Ponzi
summary: Daughter of Dick and Nancy Ponzi. Trained in Beaune and was winemaker at Ponzi Vineyards from 1993 to 2024; co-petitioner for the Laurelwood District AVA.

name: David Adelsheim
summary: Co-founded Adelsheim Vineyard with his wife Ginny after buying land near Newberg in 1971. Learned winemaking from David Lett at The Eyrie Vineyards, studied in Beaune in 1974, and co-authored the Chehalem Mountains AVA petition.

sources.title: David Adelsheim: A "Latecomer" Oregon Wine Pioneer (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Ginny Adelsheim
summary: Artist who co-founded Adelsheim Vineyard with her husband David and designed the winery's labels between 1982 and 2009.

sources.title: David Adelsheim: A "Latecomer" Oregon Wine Pioneer (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Susan Sokol Blosser
summary: Co-founded Sokol Blosser Winery in the Dundee Hills with Bill Blosser in 1971 and managed the company for 25 years before handing over to her children Alex and Alison in 2008.

name: Bill Blosser
summary: Co-founded Sokol Blosser Winery with Susan Sokol Blosser in 1971; the couple married in 1966 after graduating from Stanford.

name: Alex Sokol Blosser
summary: Son of the Sokol Blosser founders. Joined the winery full-time in 1998, became co-president in 2008, was winemaker from 2013 to 2023 and then president.

name: Alison Sokol Blosser
summary: Daughter of the Sokol Blosser founders. Joined the winery in sales and marketing in 2004 and was co-president with her brother Alex from 2008 until retiring from the role in 2023.

name: Myron Redford
summary: Bought a small vineyard in Amity in 1974 and founded Amity Vineyards, making the wines until 2008. Helped organize the Steamboat Pinot Noir Conference and the first International Pinot Noir Celebration.

sources.title: The Legacy of Steamboat (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Pat Campbell
summary: Co-founded Elk Cove Vineyards near Gaston with her husband Joe in 1974, handling management and the vineyards.

sources.title: Joe Campbell, Pioneering Willamette Valley Winemaker, Dies at 87 (Wine Spectator)

name: Joe Campbell
summary: Physician who co-founded Elk Cove Vineyards with his wife Pat in 1974 and made its wines until retiring in 1999.

sources.title: Joe Campbell, Pioneering Willamette Valley Winemaker, Dies at 87 (Wine Spectator)

name: Adam Campbell
summary: Son of Pat and Joe Campbell. Joined his parents at Elk Cove Vineyards in 1995 and took over winemaking from his father in 1999.

sources.title: Joe Campbell, Pioneering Willamette Valley Winemaker, Dies at 87 (Wine Spectator)

name: Jim Maresh
summary: Dundee Hills farmer who, with his wife Loie, bought a farm on Worden Hill Road in 1959 and began planting wine grapes in 1970 at Dick Erath's suggestion.

sources.title: Tribute to Jim Maresh (Oregon Wine Press)
Vineyards Established 1965-1971 (The PinotFile / Prince of Pinot)

name: Bill Fuller
summary: Co-founded Tualatin Vineyards near Forest Grove in 1973 and ran it until selling to Willamette Valley Vineyards in 1997, after which he continued to work with that company.

name: Mark Vlossak
summary: Founder and winemaker of St. Innocent Winery, which he started in 1988 after apprenticing under Fred Arterberry Jr. from 1987 to 1989. He was also winemaker for Panther Creek Cellars from 1994 through the 1999 harvest.

name: John Paul
summary: Founder, owner and winemaker of Cameron Winery in Dundee, which he started in 1984. He had been an assistant winemaker at Carneros Creek Winery in Napa Valley.

name: Bill Wayne
summary: Grower who planted Abbey Ridge Vineyard in the Dundee Hills with his wife Julia in the late 1970s. The Waynes are partners in Cameron Winery.

sources.title: Vineyard: Abbey Ridge (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Gary Andrus
summary: Former U.S. Olympic skier who founded Pine Ridge Vineyards in Napa and then, with Nancy Andrus, Archery Summit in the Dundee Hills. He sold Archery Summit in 2001 and later made wine under the Gypsy Dancer label; he died in 2009.

sources.title: Archery Summit Winery (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Doug Tunnell
summary: Owner of Brick House Vineyards on Ribbon Ridge, a 40-acre farm he has run organically since 1990.

sources.title: Brick House Wine Company (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Patty Green
summary: Winemaker who started at HillCrest Vineyard in 1986, worked at Adelsheim and launched Torii Mor as its first winemaker in 1993. She co-founded Patricia Green Cellars with Jim Anderson in 2000 and died in November 2017 aged 62.

sources.title: In Memoriam: Patty Green (Oregon Wine Press)

name: Jim Anderson
summary: Co-founder with Patty Green of Patricia Green Cellars, and its owner and winemaker. He worked part-time at Autumn Wind from 1993 to 1995, the property the two later bought.

sources.title: In Memoriam: Patty Green (Oregon Wine Press)
Jim Anderson Interview (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Donald Olson
summary: Physician who founded Torii Mor Winery in 1993 around his Olson vineyard in the Dundee Hills.

sources.title: Torii Mor Winery (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Don Lange
summary: Co-founder with his wife Wendy of Lange Estate Winery, established in the Dundee Hills in 1987 after they moved from Santa Barbara. He is described as among the first in the Willamette Valley to plant Pinot gris.

sources.title: Lange Estate Winery and Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Jesse Lange
summary: Son of Don and Wendy Lange, trained at Lincoln University in New Zealand and Oregon State. He took over winemaking at Lange Estate in 2005, also becoming general manager.

sources.title: Lange Estate Winery and Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Jimi Brooks
summary: Winemaker who worked at WillaKenzie Estate and Maysara before founding Brooks in 1998. He died in 2004 at 38, leaving the winery to his son Pascal.

sources.title: Brooks Wine: The People of Brooks

name: Moe Momtazi
summary: Iranian-born civil engineer who bought a wheat farm outside McMinnville with his wife Flora in 1997 and planted Momtazi Vineyard from 1998. He owns Maysara Winery and farms biodynamically.

sources.title: Moe and Hanna Momtazi interview photograph (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Denis Burger
summary: Co-owner, with Elaine McCall and David Hinrichs, of Yamhill Valley Vineyards in the McMinnville AVA, family owned since 1983.

sources.title: Yamhill Valley Vineyards (The Prince of Pinot)
Yamhill Valley Vineyards Collection (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Bernard Lacroute
summary: Burgundy-born technology executive who bought a cattle farm in the Willamette Valley in 1991 and founded WillaKenzie Estate with his wife Ronni. He sold the estate to Jackson Family Wines in 2016 to retire.

sources.title: Jackson Family Continues Oregon Pinot Noir Expansion, Buying WillaKenzie Estate (Wine Spectator)

name: Laurent Montalieu
summary: Winemaker who was a partner and winemaker at WillaKenzie Estate until 2003, when he launched NW Wine Company with John Niemeyer. He and his wife Danielle Andrus Montalieu, daughter of Gary Andrus, own Soléna and bought Hyland Vineyard in 2007.

sources.title: NW Wine Company (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Russ Raney
summary: Founder of Evesham Wood, who moved to Portland in 1983, launched the winery in 1986 and planted Le Puits Sec Vineyard. He and his wife Mary sold the winery in 2010.

sources.title: Erin Nuccio, Evesham Wood | Haden Fig (Eola-Amity Hills Winegrowers)

name: Erin Nuccio
summary: Assistant winemaker at Evesham Wood from 2007 and owner of the Haden Fig label. He and Jordan Nuccio bought Evesham Wood in August 2010, when he became head winemaker.

sources.title: Evesham Wood winery listing (The Prince of Pinot)
Erin Nuccio, Evesham Wood | Haden Fig (Eola-Amity Hills Winegrowers)

name: Melissa Burr
summary: Hired in 2003 as Stoller Family Estate's first dedicated winemaker, after an internship at Cooper Mountain Vineyards in 2001.

name: Tony Soter
summary: Winemaker who came to Napa in 1975, launched Etude in 1982 and was Spottswoode's first winemaker. He founded Soter Vineyards in Oregon with his wife Michelle in 1997, sold Etude in 2001 and moved to Oregon in 2006.

name: Ted Gerber
summary: Grower who bought land in the Illinois Valley with his wife Meri in 1971 and planted some of Southern Oregon's first wine grapes. They founded Foris Vineyards in 1986.

name: Stephen Reustle
summary: Former CPA who, with his wife Gloria, bought 200 acres in the Umpqua Valley in 2001 and started Reustle-Prayer Rock Vineyards, where he is owner and winemaker.

sources.title: 2017 Pacific Northwest Winery of the Year: Reustle Prayer Rock Vineyard (Umpqua Valley Wineries)
Reustle-Prayer Rock Vineyards Grüner Veltliner (Great Northwest Wine)

name: Eric Lemelson
summary: Reed College graduate and lawyer who planted his first vines in 1995 and founded Lemelson Vineyards.

name: Amy Wesselman
summary: Co-founder and co-winemaker of Westrey Wine Company and long-time executive director of the International Pinot Noir Celebration. She previously worked at Bethel Heights, Rex Hill and The Eyrie Vineyards.

sources.title: Westrey Wine Company (The Prince of Pinot)

name: David Autrey
summary: Co-founder and co-winemaker of Westrey Wine Company. He previously worked at Adelsheim and Cameron.

sources.title: Westrey Wine Company (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Dai Crisp
summary: Vineyard manager of Temperance Hill since 1999, where he led its replanting and organic certification. He and his wife PK McCoy founded Lumos Wine Company in 2000.

name: Dan Dusschee
summary: Owner and manager of Freedom Hill Vineyard, which he planted with his wife Helen in the early 1980s.

name: Ken Durant
summary: Co-founder and co-owner, with his wife Penny, of Durant Vineyards in the Dundee Hills, established in 1973.

name: Tim Ramey
summary: Owner with his wife Kari of Zenith Vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills, which they bought in 2002 and replanted.

name: Nancy Daniel
summary: Founder of Canary Hill Vineyard in the Eola-Amity Hills, planted from 1983. She and her husband Dick sold it to Ken Wright in 2006.

sources.title: Nancy Daniel interview photograph (Oregon Wine History Archive, Linfield)

name: Kevin Chambers
summary: Grower who planted Resonance Vineyard with his wife Carla in 1981 and co-owned Oregon Vineyard Supply and Results Partners. He was named Oregon Wine Industry Man of the Year in 2005.

sources.title: Burgundy's Louis Jadot Purchases Oregon Pinot Noir Vineyard (Wine Spectator)

name: Eric Hamacher
summary: Winemaker behind Hamacher Wines and a co-founder of the Carlton Winemakers Studio in 2002. He is married to Luisa Ponzi.

summary: Longtime Maison Louis Jadot winemaker, with more than 42 vintages at the house, who became a winemaker at its Oregon project Résonance.

name: Thibault Gagey
summary: Director of operations at Résonance. He worked a harvest in the Willamette Valley in 2012, the year before Maison Louis Jadot, whose president is Pierre-Henry Gagey, bought the Résonance Vineyard.

name: Guillaume Large
summary: Winemaker at Résonance. He was assistant technical director at Maison Louis Jadot's Burgundy headquarters before moving to Oregon in 2017.

name: Jean-Nicolas Méo
summary: Owner and winemaker of Domaine Méo-Camuzet in Burgundy, where he has worked since 1989. In 2012 he co-founded Nicolas-Jay in the Willamette Valley with his longtime friend Jay Boberg.

name: Jay Boberg
summary: Music entrepreneur who co-founded Nicolas-Jay with Jean-Nicolas Méo in 2012, after an Oregon visit in 2011 sparked the idea. The two met in 1988.

name: Casey McClellan
summary: Founder and winemaker of Seven Hills Winery. He helped his father, Dr. James McClellan, and Herb Hendricks plant Seven Hills Vineyard near Milton-Freewater in the early 1980s.

name: Steve Girard
summary: Founder, with his wife Carol, of Girard Winery in Napa Valley and later of Benton-Lane Winery in the southern Willamette Valley, on property they bought in 1988.

sources.title: Napa Valley's Huneeus Vintners Buys Oregon's Benton-Lane Winery (Wine Spectator)

name: Liz Chambers
summary: Owner, with her family, of Panther Creek Cellars from 2005 until its sale to Bacchus Capital Management in 2013.

sources.title: Wine Investment Group Makes Big Moves in Pacific Northwest (Wine Spectator)

summary: Former wine director for Michael Mina's restaurants and co-founder of Sandhi Wines in California. He and Sashi Moorman took over operations at Evening Land in 2014.

summary: California winemaker at Sandhi Wines who, with Rajat Parr, took over operations at Evening Land in 2014.

summary: Burgundy vigneron who is a partner in and consultant to Mark Tarlov's Chapter 24 Vineyards in the Willamette Valley.

summary: Co-owner of Troon Vineyard in the Applegate Valley. He and his wife Denise, from Arlington, Texas, bought it in 2017 and converted it to Biodynamic farming.

summary: Co-owner of Troon Vineyard in the Applegate Valley, which she and her husband Bryan, from Arlington, Texas, bought in 2017.

summary: General manager of Troon Vineyard, charged with converting it to Biodynamic farming. He previously worked at Cornerstone Cellars in Napa and Anne Amie in Oregon.

summary: Founder, with his wife Eileen and son Thomas, of Hood River Vineyards in 1981, the oldest winery in the Columbia Gorge.

summary: Owner and winemaker of Hood River Vineyards, which he and his wife Anne bought from the Blanchette family in 1992.

sources.title: In the sweet spot for growing fruit, Anne and Bernie Lerch enjoy staying small (Columbia Gorge News)

name: Bob Morus
summary: Founder of Phelps Creek Vineyards and Mt. Defiance Wine Company in Hood River.

name: Alexandrine Roy
summary: Fourth-generation winemaker at Domaine Marc Roy in Gevrey-Chambertin. She first made the Cuvée Alexandrine at Phelps Creek Vineyards in 2007 and took charge of all its wines from the 2012 vintage.

name: Cecil Zerba
summary: Milton-Freewater nurseryman who founded Zerba Cellars with his wife Marilyn in 2001.

summary: Californian who, with his wife Margaret, bought the Del Rio orchard property at Gold Hill in 1997 and turned it into Del Rio Vineyards.

summary: Loire Valley-born winemaker at Del Rio Vineyards, who arrived in 2008 from New York's Finger Lakes.

summary: Co-founder, with her husband Bill, of Cowhorn Vineyard & Garden in the Applegate Valley, which they sold in 2021.

summary: Leader of the investor group that bought Cowhorn Vineyard & Garden from Bill and Barbara Steele in 2021, becoming its general manager.

summary: Munich-born botanist at Oregon State and wine collector who, at 90, began the 00 Wines project with his son Chris. He has since died.

name: Nate Wall
summary: Winemaker at Troon Vineyard in the Applegate Valley since 2018, after about ten years in the Willamette Valley, including Day Wines, and time in Virginia.

name: Erik Kramer
summary: Winemaker hired by Domaine Serene in 2011.

name: David Paige
summary: Adelsheim Vineyard winemaker who worked alongside Gina Hennen for years before leaving in 2017 to start his own label, David Paige Wines.

name: CJ McCollum
summary: NBA guard, then with the Portland Trail Blazers, who launched the McCollum Heritage 91 label with Adelsheim in 2019 and in 2021 bought 318 acres in the Yamhill-Carlton AVA next to Resonance Vineyard.

name: Paul de Lancellotti
summary: Owner and grower at de Lancellotti Family Vineyards, an early adopter of biodynamic farming who credits Jimi Brooks with teaching him much about it.

name: Robert Brittan
summary: UC Davis graduate who was the first winemaker at Far Niente and spent 16 years at Stags' Leap Winery before buying land in the McMinnville foothills in 2004 for Brittan Vineyards. He also makes or consults on wine for several Willamette Valley labels.

name: Don Hagge
summary: Founder of Vidon Vineyard near Newberg, known for his experiments, including an early planting of Pinot noir clone 95 from cuttings given by Dick Erath. He and his wife Vicki sold to Dru and Erin Allen in 2020.

sources.title: Vidon Vineyard Announces New Name, Compris Vineyard (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Jessica Mozeico
summary: Co-founder, president and winemaker of Et Fille Wines, which she started with her late father Howard.

name: Michael Lundeen
summary: University of Oregon journalism graduate who began in the cellar at WillaKenzie and Domaine Serene, worked a 2005 harvest in Piedmont and studied at Chemeketa before launching Lundeen Wines. An early Oregon sparkling producer.

name: Piper Underbrink
summary: Owner of Privé Vineyard, which she bought in 2020.

name: Werner Nistler Jr.
summary: Co-founder of Amaterra with his wife Colleen; founder of the Touchmark retirement-community company.

name: Colleen Nistler
summary: Co-founder of Amaterra with her husband Werner Nistler Jr.

name: Marcus Breuer
summary: Co-founder and CEO of Amaterra and chief executive of Touchmark; a grade-school friend of winemaker Matt Vuylsteke.

name: Matt Vuylsteke
summary: Founding winemaker of Amaterra and founder of the 51Weeks label.

name: Michael Mega
summary: Owner and winemaker of Nysa Vineyard in the Dundee Hills.

name: Janie Brooks Heuck
summary: Sister of Jimi Brooks and managing director of Brooks Wine, which she has run since his death in 2004 on behalf of his son Pascal.

name: Pascal Brooks
summary: Son of Jimi Brooks, who inherited Brooks Wine at the age of eight when his father died in 2004 and remains its sole owner.

name: Bryan Laing
summary: Winemaker and co-owner of Hazelfern Cellars with his wife Laura.

name: Laura Laing
summary: Co-owner of Hazelfern Cellars with her husband Bryan.

name: Vincent Fritzsche
summary: Owner and winemaker of Vincent Wine Company, which he runs single-handed.

name: Teal Walker
summary: Proprietor of Audeant, the Willamette Valley label she created with winemaker Andrew Riechers after a tasting at Antica Terra.

name: Andrew Riechers
summary: Winemaker of Audeant since its first vintage in 2016; previously Maggie Harrison's assistant winemaker at Antica Terra.

name: Chris Mazepink
summary: Founder and winemaker of White Walnut Estate. A New Yorker who came to Oregon State in 2000, he worked at Willamette Valley Vineyards, Shea, Benton-Lane and Archery Summit, and ran his own Ebony Wines label from 2009.

name: Ximena Orrego
summary: Owner and winemaker of Atticus Wine.

name: Laura Volkman
summary: Grower and winemaker behind Laura Volkman Vineyards, mentored by Michael Etzel of Beaux Frères; she sold the property in 2012.

name: Bill Sanchez
summary: Co-owner and winemaker of Potter's Vineyard and its Vino Vasai label with his wife Sandy.

name: Sandy Sanchez
summary: Co-owner of Potter's Vineyard with her husband Bill.

name: Ron Johnson
summary: Planted Dion Vineyard with his wife Joanne from 1973 and in the 1990s wrote the first petition for a Laurelwood appellation within the Chehalem Mountains.

name: Joanne Johnson
summary: Co-founder of Dion Vineyard with her husband Ron.

name: Kevin Johnson
summary: Son of Dion Vineyard founders Ron and Joanne Johnson; a Navy and aerospace veteran who came back to make the family's wines.

name: Beth Klingner
summary: Winemaker at Dion Vineyard with her husband Kevin Johnson. A former Intel employee from Colorado, she worked weekend shifts at Archery Summit before joining Dion for the 2011 vintage.

name: Joel Myers
summary: Grower who helped plant the Letts' vineyard as a boy, became vineyard and cellar manager at Eyrie after 1979, studied with Swiss researcher Werner Koblet and founded the Vinetenders vineyard management company in 1984. Co-owner of Siltstone Wines.

name: Louise Myers
summary: Teacher and artist from a local farm family who worked at Eyrie, married Joel Myers in 1981 and runs Siltstone Wines with him.

name: Joel Sokoloff
summary: Farm and vineyard manager at Soter Vineyards from 2022, after more than seven years with Horsepower Vineyards in the Walla Walla Valley.

name: Pascal Marchand
summary: Quebec-born Burgundy winemaker, formerly at Domaine de la Vougeraie, who trained Isabelle Meunier and recommended her to Evening Land.

name: Leah Jørgensen
summary: Winemaker behind Leah Jørgensen Cellars, known for Oregon Cabernet franc. She came to Oregon Pinot Camp in 2004 and worked under Drew Voit at Shea Wine Cellars before starting her own label.

name: James Frey
summary: Winemaker at Trisaetum on Ribbon Ridge; his daughter Tatum helped start the estate's Brixeur Spirits.

name: Vince Vidrine
summary: Winemaker who worked at Irvine & Roberts and Benton-Lane before moving to Cowhorn in Southern Oregon in 2022.

name: Tresider Burns
summary: Winemaker named to lead Alexana Winery in July 2022, succeeding Bryan Weil. He previously ran winemaking at White Rose Estate and was associate winemaker at Brittan Vineyards, and also worked at Lemelson.

sources.title: Tresider Burns named winemaker for Alexana Winery (Wine Industry Advisor)

name: Chris Figgins
summary: Winemaker at Leonetti Cellar in Walla Walla and founding winemaker of Doubleback; his Toil project makes Oregon Pinot noir.

name: Matt Perry
summary: Winemaker at 00 Wines in 2022 who had left by 2025 to start a project of his own; married to Kimberly Abrahams.

name: Kimberly Abrahams
summary: Wine professional who joined Archery Summit in 2025; married to former 00 Wines winemaker Matt Perry.

name: Dave Specter
summary: Former attorney who became the winemaker and co-owner of Bells Up Winery.

name: Sara Specter
summary: Co-owner of Bells Up Winery with Dave Specter.

name: Travis Todd
summary: Winemaker and co-founder of de la boue. A former wine buyer at the Yellowstone Club in Montana, he worked harvest at Wine by Joe in 2014, moved to Oregon in 2017 and rose to head winemaker at Integrated Beverage Group in 2020.

name: Chris Andrew
summary: Co-founder of de la boue with Travis Todd, whom he met at the Yellowstone Club.

name: Antony Beck
summary: Member of the family behind South Africa's Graham Beck sparkling wine house and equal partner with Andy Lytle in Lytle-Barnett.

name: Chris Thomas
summary: Co-owner of Celestial Hill with his wife Melissa; the couple bought the former Falcon Glen vineyard near McMinnville in 2020 after first looking at property in France.

name: Melissa Thomas
summary: Co-owner of Celestial Hill with her husband Chris.

name: Jay Somers
summary: Founder of J. Christopher Wines and the first winemaker for Celestial Hill.

name: Alisa Le
summary: Winemaker who was assistant winemaker at Authentique before joining Wynne Peterson-Nedry on the Celestial Hill winemaking team in 2023.

name: Derek Einberger
summary: Winemaker at Dobbes Family Estate as of 2022.

name: John Carter
summary: Owner of Dusky Goose with Linda Carter; the couple established Rambouillet Vineyard in the Dundee Hills in 2001.

name: Linda Carter
summary: Owner of Dusky Goose with John Carter.

name: Joe Wright
summary: Head winemaker at Left Coast Estate since 2011. He started as a cellar hand at Willamette Valley Vineyards in 1996, joined Belle Vallée Cellars in 2002, and also has his own J. Wright Vintner label.

name: David O'Reilly
summary: Former owner of Owen Roe and a mentor to Steve Lutz of Lenné Estate.

name: Angelica O'Reilly
summary: Founder, with her daughters, of Distaff Wine in Newberg; wife of David O'Reilly.

name: Corby Stonebraker-Soles
summary: Co-owner and business manager of ROCO Winery with her husband Rollin Soles. She was previously married to Ken Wright and is the mother of Purple Hands winemaker Cody Wright.

sources.title: Rollin Soles and Corby Stonebraker-Soles interview (Linfield, Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Erin Percheron
summary: Winemaker at Andante Vineyard, as listed on the winery's site in early 2023.

name: Chase Renton
summary: Winemaker for L'Angolo Estate and for Chosen Family Wines.

name: Howard Mozeico
summary: Co-founder of Et Fille Wines with his daughter Jessica.

name: Andrea Lassa
summary: Co-founder of Trisaetum with her husband, winemaker James Frey.

name: Joel Kiff
summary: Co-owner of J.L. Kiff Vineyard, where he farms the vines and makes the wine.

name: Laurie Kiff
summary: Oregon-born co-owner of J.L. Kiff Vineyard with her husband Joel.

name: Carl Thoma
summary: Proprietor, with Marilynn Thoma, of Van Duzer Vineyards, which they established in 1998.

name: Marilynn Thoma
summary: Proprietor, with Carl Thoma, of Van Duzer Vineyards, which they established in 1998.

name: Janis Pate
summary: Founder and owner of Arlyn, a farm, vineyard and wine label near Newberg that she started after more than 20 years in risk management at Disney.

name: Kathy McBride
summary: Australian winemaker who travels to Oregon each harvest as assistant winemaker at Walter Scott Wines.

name: Dan Warnshuis
summary: Owner and winemaker of Utopia Vineyard. A former Silicon Valley worker and Napa wine-shop owner, he moved to Oregon in 2007 and was president of the Ribbon Ridge Winegrowers Association in 2021.

name: Andrew Dirks
summary: Director of hospitality at Abbott Claim. He started at Anne Amie, worked as a sommelier in San Francisco restaurants and was hospitality manager at Antica Terra.

name: Hollings Renton
summary: Proprietor of L'Angolo Estate with his wife Lou, and father of winemaker Chase Renton; a former biotechnology executive.

name: Lou Renton
summary: Proprietor of L'Angolo Estate with her husband Hollings, and mother of winemaker Chase Renton.

name: Jacob Gray
summary: General manager of L'Angolo Estate in 2021, who came to wine from the film industry.

name: David Nemarnik
summary: Proprietor and vineyard manager of Alloro Vineyard, which he began planting in 1999 on a hillside he used to pass on bike rides.

name: Tom Fitzpatrick
summary: Winemaker at Alloro Vineyard since 2010 and owner-winemaker of Élevée Winegrowers. He holds a master's degree in viticulture and enology from UC Davis and worked in Burgundy.

name: Sid Heinze
summary: Co-founder of King's North with his younger brother Mac.

name: Mac Heinze
summary: Co-founder of King's North with his older brother Sid.

name: Jessica Cortell
summary: Willamette Valley vineyard manager who farms Namaste Vineyard and looks after Audeant's estate planting on Parrett Mountain, and who introduces small producers to growers.

name: Tracy Kendall
summary: Associate winemaker at Nicolas-Jay from 2014, after a first harvest at Torii Mor in 2009, harvests in Australia and New Zealand and four years as enologist at Adelsheim. She later became consulting winemaker at L'Angolo Estate.

name: Jacques Tardy
summary: Burgundy-born winemaker at Torii Mor Winery, under whom Tracy Kendall worked her first harvest in 2009.

name: Wayne Bailey
summary: Farmer and winemaker who bought Youngberg Hill in 2003; the vineyard blocks are named for his daughters.

name: Rachel Rose
summary: Winemaker and vineyard manager at Bryn Mawr Vineyards. She studied viticulture and oenology in Australia and worked at Ponzi and Penner-Ash before joining the Lauers.

name: Jon Lauer
summary: Co-owner of Bryn Mawr Vineyards with his wife Kathy since 2009.

name: Kathy Lauer
summary: Co-owner of Bryn Mawr Vineyards with her husband Jon since 2009.

name: Karyn Howard Smith
summary: Director of hospitality at Bryn Mawr Vineyards from May 2018; married to winemaker Egon Smith.

name: Egon Smith
summary: Winemaker at Anne Amie Vineyards in 2021 and husband of Karyn Howard Smith.

name: Mark Hammond
summary: Co-founder of Privé Vineyard with his wife Tina; he also ran a hardware store in town.

name: Tina Hammond
summary: Co-founder and original winemaker of Privé Vineyard, which she and her husband Mark sold in 2020.

name: Tahmiene Momtazi
summary: Winemaker at Maysara Winery, who presented its 2017 Jamsheed Pinot noir at the 2021 IPNC Grand Seminar.

name: Ken Austin
summary: Owner, with his wife, of Rain Dance Vineyards and its Raindance Vineyard near the Allison Inn in Newberg.

name: Ed Walk
summary: Co-owner of Hummingbird Estate with his wife Susan, after four decades farming in Illinois.

name: Susan Walk
summary: Co-owner of Hummingbird Estate with her husband Ed.

name: Doug Irvine
summary: Co-founder of Irvine & Roberts Vineyards in Ashland.

name: Jack Day
summary: Member of the family behind Hillcrest Orchard in Medford who planted its first vines in 1997, leading to RoxyAnn Winery. He died in October 2020.

name: Rob Folin
summary: Winemaker at Belle Fiore Winery, making wine in Southern Oregon since 2005; he interned at Domaine Serene.

name: Sarah Thompson
summary: Winemaker at Cowhorn from 2021, previously assistant winemaker at Troon Vineyard.

name: Emily Gladhart
summary: Daughter of John and Lena Winter, who bought the Winter's Hill farm in 1961. With her husband Peter she planted its first grapes in 1990.

name: Peter Gladhart
summary: Planted the first grapes at Winter's Hill in 1990 with his wife Emily, after the couple took over her family's farm.

name: Russell Gladhart
summary: Son of Emily and Peter Gladhart and second-generation winemaker at Winter's Hill Estate, where he took over winemaking in 2015.

sources.title: Oregon Wine Month feature: Winter's Hill Estate (1000 Friends of Oregon)
Bees, Birds and Pinot Take Center Stage at Winter's Hill Estate (Portland Monthly, sponsored)

name: Delphine Gladhart
summary: Winemaker at Winter's Hill Estate from 2005 until 2015, when she moved to a research position with ETS Laboratories. Originally from Lyon, France, and married to Russell Gladhart.

sources.title: Bees, Birds and Pinot Take Center Stage at Winter's Hill Estate (Portland Monthly, sponsored)

name: Jesús Guillén
summary: Winemaker from Chihuahua, Mexico, who came to Oregon in 2002, rose from the vineyard and cellar to head winemaker at White Rose Estate in 2008, and built his own label, Guillén Family Wines. Described as the first Hispanic head winemaker in Oregon.

Guillén Family Wines (The Prince of Pinot)

name: Jesús Guillén Sr.
summary: Came to Oregon from Chihuahua in 2000 and became vineyard manager at White Rose Estate. Father of winemaker Jesús Guillén, and planter of the family's Domingo Vineyard.

sources.title: Guillén Family Wines (The Prince of Pinot)
Jesús Guillén Olvera (1980–2018): Réquiem para un gentilhombre (Oregon Wine Press)
